ideas.pitch: A real-time mobile app designed to help teams track active chaotic curveballs, unexpected non-tech elimination tasks, and coordinate rapid countermeasures during unpredictable hackathon rounds.
ideas.title: ChaosCompanion
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the specific Chaos & Plot Twist theme of Triwizathon by giving teams a tactical advantage during surprise elimination rounds, aligning with the event's fun and unpredictable spirit.

ideas.pitch: An AI-assisted prompt generator and strategy router that helps teams rapidly brainstorm and structure solutions when hit with surprise rule changes or sudden problem mutations.
ideas.title: TwistDraft
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly tackles the surprise challenge element where teams must think on their feet and pivot instantly, proving highly valuable when judges introduce mid-hackathon plot twists.

ideas.pitch: A gamified treasure-hunt platform that automates non-tech puzzle checkpoints and verification for multi-stage hybrid events.
ideas.title: RiddleRouter
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the unique hybrid and non-tech challenge angle of Triwizathon, functioning as a meta-tool that organizers or teams can use to manage chaotic elimination rounds.

ideas.pitch: An agile micro-kanban board optimized for 4-member teams facing sudden time constraints and high-pressure elimination rounds.
ideas.title: TaskTango
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses heavily on flawless team execution under extreme time pressure and sudden format changes, ensuring the 4-member squad stays perfectly synchronized.

ideas.pitch: A collaborative simulation game where teams practice rapid pivoting and handling unexpected constraints under simulated hackathon chaos.
ideas.title: SabotageShield
ideas.why_it_could_win: Captures the fun-over-pressure ethos of the event with a working, highly entertaining live demo that judges can interact with directly.
